evals.prompt: Generame el test unitario para un Use Case 'ProcessOrder' que depende de un 'OrderRepository' y un 'PaymentService'. El PaymentService devuelve un Result (neverthrow).
evals.expected_output: The skill MUST generate a Fishery Factory for Order, an InMemoryOrderRepository, and a test suite with a setup() function. The naming MUST use natural language ('should X when Y'). It MUST include AAA comments and use Result type assertions (isOk, isErr, _unsafeUnwrap).

assertions.description: Must include at least 3 test cases: happy path, entity not found, and business logic error

expectations: Defines setup() returning the fake, the mock, and the use case
Uses an InMemoryOrderRepository instead of mocking OrderRepository
Every test has // Arrange, // Act, // Assert comments
Asserts Result outcomes with isOk()/isErr()
Covers happy path, order not found, and payment failure

evals.prompt: Create unit tests for 'UserRegistration' use case. It depends on 'UserRepository' and 'EmailService'. Use exceptions for error handling.
evals.expected_output: The skill MUST generate the Factory, the InMemoryUserRepository, and tests that use rejects.toThrow for error cases. The setup() function must return Fakes and mocks. Assertions should verify repository state when applicable.

assertions.description: Must verify persisted state in the InMemory repository, not just mock call verification

expectations: Defines setup() and an InMemoryUserRepository fake
Uses rejects.toThrow for error cases
Verifies persisted user via repository.findById
Mocks EmailService rather than faking it
Test names follow 'should ... when ...'

evals.expected_output: The skill must handle 3+ dependencies correctly: Fake for AccountRepository, mock for TransactionLogger and FraudDetectionService. Must generate setup() returning all three plus the SUT. Tests must cover: successful transfer, insufficient funds, fraud detected.

assertions.description: setup() must return at least 4 items: repository, transactionLogger, fraudDetectionService, useCase
Must include test for fraud detection failure path using Result type assertions

expectations: Uses InMemoryAccountRepository, not a mock, for AccountRepository
Uses mock<TransactionLogger>() and mock<FraudDetectionService>()
setup() returns repository, logger, fraud service, and use case
Covers success, insufficient funds, and fraud detected
Asserts balances through the fake repository

Must include a test that overrides specific LineItem data using .build() with nested overrides

evals.prompt: Mi proyecto usa Vitest. Generame tests para un use case 'CancelSubscription' que depende de 'SubscriptionRepository' y 'BillingGateway'. Usa Result types.
evals.expected_output: The skill MUST detect Vitest from the user's statement and use vitest-mock-extended import instead of jest-mock-extended. All other patterns (setup, AAA, Fakes, naming) must remain the same.

assertions.description: Must use 'vitest-mock-extended' import, never 'jest-mock-extended', since user specified Vitest

expectations: Imports from vitest-mock-extended and never jest-mock-extended
Uses vi (not jest) for any timer or mock helpers
Defines setup() with an InMemory subscription repository
Asserts Result with isOk()/isErr()
Covers subscription not found and billing failure

evals.prompt: Escribe los tests unitarios para el use case 'RedeemPasswordResetToken'. Depende de 'ResetTokenRepository' y 'UserRepository'. El token expira 30 minutos después de emitirse y el use case compara contra new Date(). Usa Jest y excepciones.
evals.expected_output: The skill MUST make time deterministic: fixed system time with jest.useFakeTimers().setSystemTime, or an injected Clock. Tests cover valid token, expired token, and token exactly at expiry, with fake timers restored in afterEach. Factory uses fixed dates and a seeded Faker.
expectations: Uses jest.useFakeTimers with setSystemTime or an injected Clock port
Does not use the real current time for expected values
Covers a valid token, an expired token, and a token exactly at the expiry boundary
Restores timers in afterEach (jest.useRealTimers)
Uses InMemoryResetTokenRepository and setup() with AAA comments

evals.prompt: Generate Vitest tests for 'ChargeSubscription' use case. It calls 'PaymentGateway.charge' and retries up to 3 times with exponential backoff (1s, 2s, 4s) when the gateway throws a TimeoutError. Depends on 'SubscriptionRepository' and 'PaymentGateway'. Use exceptions.
evals.expected_output: The skill MUST use vi.useFakeTimers and advance timers (advanceTimersByTimeAsync) instead of real waiting, await all promises, and cover eventual success after retries and failure after the retries are exhausted.
expectations: Uses vi.useFakeTimers and vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync (or equivalent), no real sleeps
Awaits every async call and uses rejects.toThrow for the exhausted case
Asserts the gateway charge call count for retry behavior
Covers success after a transient failure and failure after retries are exhausted
Imports vitest-mock-extended and restores real timers in afterEach

evals.prompt: Write Jest tests for 'RegisterCustomer' use case. Input has email, phone, taxId and age. There are many invalid inputs: malformed emails, empty or too short phone, taxId with wrong check digit, age below 18 or above 120. Depends on 'CustomerRepository'. Use exceptions.
evals.expected_output: The skill MUST group the invalid inputs in a declarative it.each table with named rows, with no if/for inside the test body, plus a happy path test and a duplicate-email case.
expectations: Uses it.each or test.each with a table of invalid inputs
Table rows are named (a name field or $name in the title)
No if, for, or ternary inside any test body
Includes boundary values for age (17, 18, 120, 121)
Has a happy path persisted in InMemoryCustomerRepository and uses setup() with AAA comments

evals.prompt: Generate Vitest tests for 'PlaceOrder' use case with Result types. Flow: reserve stock via 'InventoryService', save order in 'OrderRepository', then notify via 'NotificationService'. Test what happens when InventoryService.reserve throws mid-flow, and when NotificationService throws after the order is saved.
evals.expected_output: The skill MUST cover dependency-throws and partial-failure cases: when reserve throws no order is persisted; when notification throws the outcome is defined and state stays consistent. Assertions verify the InMemory repository state, not only mock calls.
expectations: Has a test where InventoryService.reserve rejects and asserts no order exists in the fake repository
Has a test where NotificationService rejects after save and asserts the defined outcome and repository state
Uses InMemoryOrderRepository and mocks the other ports
Does not assert call order between ports
Imports vitest-mock-extended and uses setup() with AAA comments
